questions.question: What is the location of the sinoatrial node?

suspectLines.text: The source explanation describes the sinoatrial node as lying in the upper part of the crista terminalis at the junction of the superior vena cava opening and the right atrium, at the junction between the parts of the right atrium derived from the sinus venosus and primitive atrium. The question, however, presents answer combinations using numbers 1-5 without showing the numbered definitions on the rendered question page. The printed answer key marks option D.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is false regarding the SA node?

options.text: It is located at the right border of ascending aorta
It contains specialized nodal cardiac muscle
It is supplied by the atrial branches of the right coronary artery
Action potential generated here does not have phase 1 or 2

suspectLines.text: The false statement is that the sinoatrial node is located at the right border of the ascending aorta. The source places the SA node at the opening of the superior vena cava into the right atrium. It contains specialized nodal cardiac muscle and acts as the pacemaker, is supplied by atrial branches of the right coronary artery, and its action potential lacks phases 1 and 2.
